minor.comment: `Tabs` now implements the ARIA tabs pattern: one tab stop with a roving `tabIndex`, arrow keys that follow the writing direction and wrap, `Home` and `End`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` tying each tab to its panel, and a focusable panel. A new `activation` prop selects between selection-follows-focus, the default, and manual activation for panels expensive enough that arrowing past them should not render them. **A typical import drops from 2.8 KB to 0.9 KB**: a member expression at module scope made the theme objects unconditional side effects, so an application importing one component shipped both themes and the whole palette. The typical-import budget is tightened to 1.2 KB, between the shakeable 0.9 KB and the 1.5 KB a hoisted member expression costs, so the regression cannot return unnoticed.

Close the gaps consuming projects had been working around. `Button` gains a `danger` variant, an `lg` size that meets the 44px touch target, a `loading` state that keeps its width and its accessible name, and `pressed` for toggles. `Badge` gains the four status kinds, sharing `Callout`'s vocabulary. `Card` gains `tone="subtle"`. A `Label` component ships and `.yl-label` is styled standalone, so the class works where the package's own documentation said it would. `Table` cells take `numeric` for right-aligned tabular figures, and `TableScroll` provides a labelled horizontal scroll region. `Tooltip` supplies `tabIndex` so a non-focusable trigger still opens it. The five overlay hooks that shipped inside the bundle and were exported by neither entry point are now exported from `/client`. An unclassed anchor inside `.yl-root` finally reads `--yl-color-fg-link`, which was defined from the first release and applied to nothing.

Tighten the default density by one step on the 4px grid: a primary button is 36px tall rather than 44px, and card, modal, popover, table and the default layout gaps come down with it. The spacing scale itself is unchanged. Add an `interactive.track` role for the unfilled part of a control, and fix a switch whose white knob sat on a pale track at 1.48:1 when WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3:1. Derive the dark theme's surfaces from the brand pair, carbon and the deepest brand blue, instead of four hand-picked literals.

Five new exports, each one a component a consuming project had already built for itself: `Stat` and `StatGrid` for a labelled figure, which renders a real zero rather than a dash because "unavailable" and "none" are different facts; `Chip` for a compact tag, squared off so it does not read as a `Badge`; `ProgressBar`, the determinate counterpart to `Spinner`, which clamps its value, requires a `label` and fills from the inline start in both writing directions; and `AuthCard`, pure composition for a sign-in screen, rendering as `main` unless told otherwise. Plus `useControllableState`, for a value that is either the caller's or the component's, and `noFlashScript()`, the inline script that restores the theme before the first paint — documented since the first release and never shipped. It shares `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` with `ThemeProvider`, so the two cannot drift.

**Breaking.** Rework the token layer into primitives, semantic roles and component locals. Thirty-eight `--yl-*` properties are renamed; `scripts/token-rename-map.json` is the full map and `scripts/codemod-tokens.mjs` applies it. The emitter now walks the token objects exhaustively instead of naming each property, which brings the twelve-style type scale, `motion.duration.slow`, two easings and the full interactive role set into CSS for the first time: 160 properties where there were 86. Brand-coloured text and button fills move from `primary[500]` to `primary[600]`, fixing a 4.06:1 contrast failure that affected every primary button label, and `tests/contrast.test.ts` now computes every pairing in both themes. No component name appears in the global token namespace any more: `btn` became `interactive`, `ghost` became `interactive-quiet`, and `code` became the `ink` surface.

Every component now reads tokens. 121 hardcoded values become 12, and each of those twelve is a deliberately relative `em`, a documented fallback, a test-pinned breakpoint or a SASS default argument. The type scale reaches CSS for the first time, reconciled to the sizes the components already rendered rather than the reverse, so nothing grows; `Typography.scss` alone drops from 26 literals to 4. A `type()` mixin applies a whole role. `CodeBlock`'s copy button derives from the ink roles instead of five hand-copied `rgba()` literals, so it finally changes with the theme. Bespoke geometry becomes named component-local properties rather than anonymous numbers. stylelint closes it: a hex, an `rgba()`, a literal font size or a literal font weight is now a lint error.

patch.comment: Give every component its own README beside its source, with examples, props and the accessibility contract, and a test that fails if a new component arrives without one. Documents four gaps found while writing them: `Tabs` sets the ARIA tab roles but implements none of the keyboard pattern, `Menu` has no typeahead, `Table` has no responsive container or numeric alignment, and there is no accordion.

`ThemeProvider` no longer breaks where storage does. Restoring a theme fell through to `data-theme="false"` when `localStorage` was absent, threw outright when reading it was blocked, and applied a stored value verbatim even when it named no theme. Reading is now guarded and validated, and persisting is allowed to fail on its own: a theme the reader chose and can see is worth more than the promise of remembering it.

The 0.3.x to 0.4.0 codemod and its rename map now ship in the package. The README has documented `node node_modules/@yoltra/ds/scripts/codemod-tokens.mjs` since the rename landed, and `scripts/` was not in `files`, so the one command a consumer needs in order to upgrade was the one command that could not run. Verified by unpacking a real tarball and running it.

Restructure the SASS. Every component stylesheet now imports one shared entry partial rather than six of fifteen importing a mixins file directly, and the fragments that were copied between them become mixins: the reduced-motion media query, two disabled treatments, the house transition and the elevated-surface treatment the modal and anchored tiers each had a private copy of. `form.css` becomes self-sufficient: `.yl-field` moves to the file whose component renders it, so `FormField` no longer silently needs `field.css` as well. A disabled checkbox now fades like the switch and slider it sits beside.

none.comment: README: a table of the tokens that get rewritten by hand rather than read — `--yl-z-*`, `--yl-elevation-*`, `--yl-motion-*`, `--yl-breakpoint-*`, `--yl-container-*`, `--yl-font-numeric`, `--yl-font-weight-*` and `--yl-border-width-*`. Colour discipline looks after itself; none of these had a single use across the projects surveyed for this release. Also corrects the authoring path, which still described the flat layout replaced two milestones ago.

The README names every export: `MenuItem`, `MenuSeparator`, `focusableWithin` and `resolvePlacement` join the inventory. Authoring describes the shared SASS entry and all ten mixins instead of the three that predate it, and states the stylelint rule against hardcoded colours and type. The tokens section introduces the interactive track role. The Spanish README gains the `ThemeProvider` note it was missing. "Upgrading from 0.3.x" states the tighter default density, which no codemod touches. The ThemeProvider README documents `defaultTheme`, `noFlashScript()` and storage failure, and stops saying the no-flash script does not ship. The `storageKey` option of `noFlashScript` said it must match whatever `ThemeProvider` was given, but the provider takes no key and always uses `THEME_STORAGE_KEY`; its documentation now says to leave it unset beside the provider and when setting it is right. `#0F172A` is called carbon everywhere, as the dark theme already did, since `ink` now names the always-dark code surface.

Add npm version, downloads, types and licence badges to both READMEs, and set `repository.directory` so relative links in the published README resolve to this package's directory rather than the repository root.
Add snapshot coverage for the compiled stylesheets and the rendered DOM. Tests only, with no change to what the package ships.

patch.comment: Trims the licence banner to package, version, copyright holder and licence. It previously restated the MIT terms in prose and pointed at the LICENSE file, which every tarball already ships through `prepublishOnly`, and core, react and ds carried two more lines than devtools-protocol and devtools-server did. `@yoltra/core`'s `{ createStore }` goes from 9.1 KB to 9.0 KB gated, `@yoltra/react`'s barrel from 5.6 KB to 5.5 KB and 3.4 KB to 3.3 KB shipped, and `@yoltra/ds`'s barrel from 5.4 KB to 5.3 KB. Generates the published size table in this package's README instead of maintaining it by hand. `rushx size:write` rewrites it in both languages and `rushx size` fails when the committed table stops matching the measurement, which previously only `@yoltra/core` did. A row measured from a secondary entry point now names it, so `@yoltra/ds` no longer produces two different rows both labelled "everything": its `/client` barrel and its main barrel are separate numbers and now read that way.

none.comment: Adds explicit extensions to the relative specifiers of published declaration files. Extensionless relative re-exports do not resolve under `moduleResolution: nodenext`, and because nearly every project sets `skipLibCheck: true` the errors were suppressed while every re-exported symbol silently degraded to `any`.

Development dependencies only: vite 7.1.11 to 7.3.6 and vitest 3.2.4 to 3.2.7 (with @vitest/coverage-v8 where it is used), closing advisories for arbitrary file read through the dev server websocket, a `server.fs.deny` bypass via queries, path traversal in optimized-deps map handling, and a critical vitest advisory. Neither package appears in published output, so nothing this package ships changes.

minor.comment: Builds every published bundle for es2022 instead of es2019 or es2020. Class fields now emit natively rather than through a downlevel helper: `@yoltra/core` alone carried 55 `__publicField` calls plus a helper preamble that every consumer paid for on every import. `{ createStore }` drops from 9.3 KB to 9.1 KB minified and gzipped, the persistence and barrel imports and `@yoltra/react` each drop 0.1 KB, and `@yoltra/ds`'s client barrel drops 0.1 KB. No source changed and the emitted declaration files are byte-identical, so behaviour, design and type inference are untouched. The floor this sets (Chrome 94, Safari 15.4, Firefox 93, all shipped by early 2022) is one the suite already required in practice: anything depending on core inherits core's target, so the lower numbers elsewhere advertised support the suite could not deliver.

Adds the form and action tier: `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `Slider`, `FormField`, `Fieldset`, `IconButton` and `ButtonGroup`.

Every control is a native element, tinted with accent-color rather than replaced. A div dressed as a checkbox has to re-implement keyboard handling, the indeterminate state, form participation and every assistive-technology behaviour the native control already has, and usually re-implements only some of them.

FormField hands its child the wiring through a render function rather than cloning it: the id, the aria-describedby pointing at hint and error, and aria-invalid. Cloning reads more tidily and breaks the moment a caller wraps their control in a fragment or a component of their own, because the props land on the wrapper and nothing reports it. The error region is always rendered and carries role=alert, so a message appearing after a failed submit reaches a reader who has already moved past the field.

Fieldset and RadioGroup use a real fieldset and legend, the one construct that gets a group name announced before each control inside it. RadioGroup does not set the shared name on its children, for the same reason FormField does not clone: it is documented instead. Switch is a checkbox carrying role=switch, which is what makes a reader hear on and off rather than checked and unchecked. Slider takes a valueText for scales where the bare number says nothing. IconButton requires its label and renders it visually hidden, because an icon button with no accessible name is announced as 'button' and nothing else — so the component does not offer the option of omitting it.

Adds fifteen primitives: `Stack`, `Inline`, `Grid`, `Container`, `Divider`, `Card`, `Heading`, `Text`, `Link`, `InlineCode`, `Kbd`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` and `VisuallyHidden`.

Spacing is passed per instance as a custom property rather than through modifier classes. Fourteen scale steps across five layout components would be seventy rules shipped to every consumer; one declaration reading a variable is a single rule, and still loses to a class the caller writes.

The accessibility decisions live in the API rather than being left to each call site. Spinner announces through a status role with a visually-hidden label defaulting to 'Loading', because an indicator nobody can perceive is worse than none. Skeleton is hidden from assistive technology, since announcing a row of grey boxes tells a screen-reader user nothing they can act on. Heading takes a visual size independent of its outline level, so a section that should look small stays the heading it structurally is, and EmptyState takes a configurable heading level for the same reason. Divider is an hr horizontally and a separator role vertically, because a thematic break turned on its side is not one. Link applies noopener with a blank target, which is a hole rather than a preference. Both animations stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

The package also gains TypeDoc, which it never had: eighty-five pages generated with no warnings, every component carrying a worked example. Types referenced by public props but never exported — button variant and size, callout kind, field size, alignment, the theme context — are now exported, since a prop whose type cannot be named is a prop nobody can type against.

Add the anchored overlay tier: `Popover`, `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSeparator`, `ContextMenu` and `Tooltip`, plus the pure `resolvePlacement` they position with.

Unlike the modal tier these are non-modal — they sit beside the page rather than over it, so they trap nothing and lock nothing. They close on Escape, on an outside press, and when focus leaves for something that is neither the surface nor its trigger. `Menu` adds the menu keyboard pattern: focus moves to the first item on open and roves with the arrows, Home and End, wrapping at both ends, while Tab closes and continues past the trigger.

Each takes a `trigger` render prop and hands it the ARIA wiring rather than documenting it. `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` are the step that gets skipped, and a screen reader then describes a button that appears to do nothing. `aria-controls` is only emitted while the surface exists, so it never dangles.

A disabled `MenuItem` carries `aria-disabled` rather than the `disabled` attribute, so the arrow keys still reach it: being told an action is unavailable is better than being unable to find out it exists.

`Tooltip` is uncontrolled, because a tooltip's visibility belongs to the pointer and the focus ring rather than to application state. It never takes focus, is wired with `aria-describedby` rather than `aria-label` — labelling with one leaves an icon button whose name vanishes with the tooltip — and stays off the shared dismissal stack so it cannot swallow an Escape meant for a dialog underneath it.

`resolvePlacement` is exported and pure. It flips only when the opposite side actually fits; flipping to whichever side merely has more room moves an overlay taller than the window for a few percent of visible area and makes the position unpredictable. Clamping is cross-axis only, since clamping the main axis would slide the overlay over the element it describes. Coordinates are viewport-relative against `position: fixed`, so no offset-parent arithmetic is involved.

The `/client` size budget rises from 4 KB to 5.5 KB to match. `{ Dialog }` on its own did not move, which is the tree-shaking claim holding as the tier grew.

Add the modal overlay tier: `Portal`, `Dialog` and `Drawer`, published from `@yoltra/ds/client`.

Overlays render into a node under `document.body` rather than where they are written, because rendering in place loses to CSS three ways that no `z-index` fixes: an ancestor with `overflow: hidden` clips the panel, an ancestor with `transform`, `filter` or `will-change` becomes the containing block for `position: fixed` so a viewport-centred dialog is centred in that ancestor instead, and an ancestor that established a stacking context traps the overlay beneath whatever sits above it.

A new `zIndex` scale joins the foundation tokens and emits as `--yl-z-*`. Portalled surfaces land in the document's stacking order, so their order depends on nothing but these numbers; the scale encodes containment, with a popover above a dialog and a tooltip above both.

The surfaces are controlled — `open` and `onClose` are the whole state contract — and carry the behaviour that separates a usable overlay from a visible one: focus trapped inside and restored on close, page scroll locked under a reference count so nesting cannot leave it stuck, and Escape and outside-press dismissal routed through a shared stack so one keystroke closes one layer rather than every layer listening at once.

`title` is required rather than optional: a modal with no accessible name is announced as "dialog" and nothing else.

The size budget now measures the `/client` entry, which nothing checked before, and the CSS invariant test scans the overlay stylesheets alongside the primitives.

Component styles move from a generated string to SASS, and ship as one stylesheet per component.

`themeCss()` used to return the custom properties *and* every component's rules, so an application importing one Button shipped the styles for the table, the tabs and the code block as well. The JavaScript tree-shakes; a single stylesheet cannot. Styles are now authored in SASS under `src/primitives/<Component>.scss` and compiled to `dist/styles/<component>.css`, imported individually. `all.css` carries everything for consumers who would rather not choose.

SASS never owns a value: colours, spacing and radii are read as `var(--yl-*)`, because theming is a runtime `data-theme` switch and a SASS variable compiles away before that switch can reach it. What it contributes is nesting, per-component files, and shared mixins for the focus ring, visually-hidden text and breakpoints.

Lengths are now emitted in `rem` against a 10px root — `base.css` sets `html { font-size: 62.5% }`, so `--yl-space-4` is `1.6rem`. Tokens stay authored in pixels and only the output carries the unit. Breakpoints and hairline borders deliberately stay in pixels: `rem` in a media query resolves against the initial root rather than this one, and a 1px border should not invite sub-pixel rounding. `base-no-root.css` omits the root declaration for an application that sets its own.

**Breaking**: `themeCss()` no longer includes component styles. Replace a single call with the token and base sheets plus the components in use, or with `all.css`.

Open the table subcomponents to their native attributes: THead, TBody, TR, TH and TD accepted only children, so a header cell could not carry scope — the attribute that lets assistive technology associate a data cell with its header — and a cell could not span columns without dropping to a raw element. Each now extends its proper HTML attribute type and spreads, matching how every other primitive in the package already behaves, and TH's docs say why scope is not optional in spirit.

patch.comment: Declares a bundle-size budget, checked by `rush size` against the package bundled the way a consumer ships it — tree-shaken, minified and gzipped — rather than against the unminified file in `dist`, which measures nothing anybody downloads.

Tests the design system, which had none.

110 tests at 96.1% statements and 93.9% branches, with thresholds set at that floor. They cover every component's rendered element and class composition, the accessibility wiring for the form tier, the two interactive components behind the client entry, and the token and theme invariants.

The one worth naming is a stylesheet invariant: every var(--yl-*) a compiled component reads must be a property the token emitter defines. A typo in a custom property does not fail anything — it compiles, ships, and renders as though the declaration were absent, on one component, in one theme. Writing the check found exactly that: --yl-color-bg-surface never existed, so every Card fell through to its fallback and rendered the same colour as the page behind it. The theme defines bg-panel for precisely this, and Card now uses it.

Two more dead fallbacks went the same way. The rule is now that anything in a token namespace must resolve whether or not it has a fallback; only component-local properties, which a component sets per instance, may be undefined.

The size budget is re-based and split: a typical four-component import is 2.4 KB against a 5.4 KB barrel, and the gap between them is the tree-shaking claim being checked rather than asserted.

Add Input, Select, and Textarea form primitives — server-safe React components (with `size` and `block` props) plus `.yl-input` / `.yl-select` / `.yl-textarea` styles emitted by themeCss(): padding, border, background, a themed placeholder, hover, a brand focus ring, and disabled state, with `--sm` / `--block` modifiers and a `.yl-field` / `.yl-label` helper.

minor.comment: Initial release of @yoltra/ds — the Yoltra Design System, the shared visual language for the website, documentation, and examples. Ships foundation tokens (a 10-step color palette anchored on brand blue #1A7FE2, typography on Inter + JetBrains Mono, and spacing / radius / elevation / motion scales), light and dark semantic themes that map those primitives to intent-based roles (background / foreground / border / interactive / status), a themeCss() generator that emits --yl-* CSS custom properties for both themes plus base component styles, and primitive React components: Button, ButtonLink, Badge, Callout, Table (with THead/TBody/TR/TH/TD), CodeBlock, and Tabs. Theming is driven entirely by a data-theme attribute on the document root, so components resolve colors through CSS variables and render on the server without a React context.

patch.comment: Split interactive components behind a dedicated "@yoltra/ds/client" subpath entry (ThemeProvider, useTheme, applyTheme, CodeBlock, Tabs) that carries the "use client" directive, so the default "@yoltra/ds" entry stays safe to import from React Server Components (for themeCss() and the static primitives). The package "exports" map declares both "." and "./client", each with types + import + require conditions.
